The characters read *Tu-xwā-ra: every segment of Bactr. *Toxwār- is written, including the w that Skt. Tukhāra lacks; 模 for Bactr. o is regular (cf. 胡 for Gōz-)
proposed_form: *Tuxwār(a) (Bactr. *Toxwār-, τοχοαρ- in τοχοαραστανο; Sogd. ʾtxwʾrk); Skt. Tukhāra is the Sanskritised form
note: Sims-Williams derives τοχοαραστανο from *τοχοαρο "Tocharian" + -στανο (Henning 1938; Syriac thwrstn in the Xian inscription; Arabic/NP Tuxaristan). The w is the decisive point: 貨 is 合口 and the key reads it khwā in Khwārizm, so 覩貨邏 follows the Iranian *Tuxwār, not Skt. Tukhāra (which would need an open 開口 syllable). The old 吐火羅 has the same 合口 曉 syllable (火 xwa), so XZ's 訛 must concern 吐 (aspirated tʰ) against 覩 (t). Same name for 12.22.15 覩貨邏故國.
